💡 Key Takeaways
  • As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.
  • "A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.
  • The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.

"A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.

The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.

According to recent reports, mohammadi wrote the autobiography in prison: "She was constantly writing," says Claren, whose own mother, activist Nahid Taghavi, shared a cell with Mohammadi for two and a half years, in Iran's notorious Evin prison. "Then, in 2020, Narges was forcibly moved to another prison. All her documents were gone. And she had to start all over.".

But she managed to rewrite it all, and her texts were smuggled out of prison in fragments by fellow prisoners and visitors who risked their own safety.

In her memoir, Mohammadi recounts pivotal moments in her life, including her childhood and youth, how she started taking action against gender discrimination, political repression, the death penalty and human rights abuses, and the personal and emotional toll of her activism.

The human rights activist has been sentenced to a combined total of more than 44 years in prison and 154 lashes. For more than a decade, she has been separated from her twin children, who are now 19 years old and live in exile in France for their own protection.

Born on April 21, 1972, in Zanjan, Iran, Narges Mohammadi became politically active while studying in physics at Imam Khomeini University of Qazvin in the 1990s.

Industry observers note that in "A Woman Never Stops Fighting," she describes how she started mountain climbing as a student, and organized mixed-gender groups dedicated to mountaineering — a controversial initiative at the time. She also helped establish an independent student organization and advocated for political reform. Her activities led to repeated harassment and arrests by authorities.

She began her journalism career in 1996, writing about Iran's student and women's movements. As her public profile grew, she became increasingly involved in Iran's civil society and human rights community.

Sources indicate that in 1998, she married political activist Taghi Rahmani. The couple's twins, Ali and Kiana, were born in 2006.

Over the course of her career, Mohammadi worked with some of Iran's most prominent human rights organizations and became a leading figure in the Defenders of Human Rights Centre, founded by 2003 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Shirin Ebadi.

Sources indicate that she played a key role in initiatives promoting free elections, peace and the abolition of the death penalty, especially for juvenile offenders. She also helped establish organizations supporting political prisoners and advocating for women's rights.

Her first major prison sentence related to her human rights activities came in 2011. It marked the beginning of a cycle of arrests and prosecutions that would define much of her adult life.

Recent findings suggest that in her memoir, she describes an arrest that took place in front of her young children. At one point during her imprisonment, she lost the right to call them for several months.

She also details the brutal treatment she experienced in prison, with constant interrogations, beatings and denial of medical care.

Another central focus of her activism is denouncing the psychological effects of solitary confinement, which she had previously documented with fellow inmates in her book and documentary project "White Torture.".

According to recent reports, "When someone is subjected to physical torture, the scars, blood and infections — dreadful as they may be — serve as visible witnesses," she writes in her memoir. But, she adds, "when someone is subjected to psychological torture, no visible traces remain, and the victim cannot justify the trauma — neither to themselves nor to others. In fact, it becomes virtually impossible to even accept that one has been tortured at all, which causes the suffering to continue indefinitely.".

"This is also the goal of solitary confinement: to bring the imprisoned person to the very edge of nothingness — to strip them of their identity and of everything that makes them human," she writes.

Through her relentless campaigning against executions and state violence, she helped bring these problems to the forefront of public debate among Iranian activists.

International recognition of her work culminated in October 2023 when she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "for her fight against the oppression of women in Iran and her fight to promote human rights and freedom for all.".

As Mohammadi was unable to attend the ceremony because she remained imprisoned in Tehran's Evin Prison, the award was accepted on her behalf by her teenage twins, who delivered her message to the world.

Following the Nobel Prize, Iranian authorities continued to pursue fresh legal cases against her, restrict her communications and intensify pressure on her from prison.

She became the target of a systematic smear campaign, including widespread defamation, gender-based harassment and explicit death threats.

"We are firmly convinced that the Islamic Republic of Iran has deployed its cyber army — which is the second-largest, after Russia's — to this end," claims Claren of the Narges Mohammadi Foundation. Conspiracy theorists even started claiming she might be working for the regime, she adds: "And what is truly terrible about this is that when a lie is repeated over and over again and spread over the course of years, it eventually leads even ordinary people to start believing it.".

Sources indicate that in late 2024, following surgery, Mohammadi was granted a temporary medical release. Doctors warned at the time that a return to prison could seriously endanger her health.

Nevertheless, Mohammadi was brutally arrested again in December 2025, while attending a memorial ceremony for Khosrow Alikordi, a lawyer and human rights activist who died in suspicious circumstances.

Industry observers note that in prison, she was held in solitary confinement for an extended period and her health continued to deteriorate, Claren reports. But "thanks to a public campaign, she has now been granted what is known as an interruption of detention for medical reasons.".

But "that doesn't mean she is free," adds Claren, who notes that she still suffers from serious health problems — as do many Iranians who have been tortured in prison.

In February, an Iranian court ordered additional prison sentences for Mohammadi, along with a travel ban.

In a recent development, mohammadi lives in constant fear of having to return to prison any day, notes Claren, and "this all comes with the pressure to which Iranian civil society — including, of course, people like Narges — is right now subjected, with questions like: Will Trump launch an attack, yes or no? Will there be another war?".

It has been revealed that despite this uncertainty, Mohammadi continues her activism. Her international profile also helps her supporters keep addressing publicly the concern of human rights in Iran in the public eye, says Claren: "It is incredibly important that, alongside the individual Narges Mohammadi, the focus also remains consistently on the struggle of the people in Iran for freedom, dignity, and fundamental rights — for the right to sing and dance.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gareth Bale had a long and distinguished career, winning some of football's biggest prizes.

With an honours list as long as his - five UEFA Champions League winners' medals, three La Liga titles, three UEFA Super Cup wins, three Club World Cup triumphs, a Copa del Rey, a Supercopa de Espana and an English League Cup - he is certainly among those who can be considered to be among the greatest football players of all time.

It was not only domestically where he showed his class either, as he guided Wales to Euro 2016, Euro 202 and then the World Cup in 2022, with the nation reaching the semi-finals of the 2016 tournament.

Sources indicate that wales getting to the finals of significant tournaments was unheard of, with their appearance at the 2022 World Cup the nation's first since 1958. The 2016 Euros was their first ever at the UEFA tournament, with Bale at the centre of the country managing to create history.

In a recent development, during his career he has shared a pitch with some extraordinary players. With Real Madrid he played alongside Ballon d'Or winners Cristiano Ronaldo and Luka Modric, with whom he also played for Tottenham Hotspur, where he also shared the grass with current Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane.

So he has a big pool of players from which to choose the greatest teammate he has ever had.

Yet none of those three, who have won the biggest and best individual prize football has to offer are who he went for. Instead, he went with one of his countrymen, one of the greatest Premier League players of all time in Ryan Giggs.

Speaking in 2016, Bale told Foot Locker: "For me, the greatest player is Ryan Giggs. He was my hero growing up and is a legend in world football. It also helps he's a fellow Welshman.".

In fairness to Bale, he had not played with Kane by then, with his stint with the Bayern Munich striker coming when he was getting towards the end of his career, when he went back on loan to Spurs from Real Madrid in 2020/21.

Recent findings suggest that incredibly, Bale and Giggs only shared the pitch on three occasions. They first played together in 2006/07 during a friendly against Brazil, before then playing together in European Championship qualifiers in 2007/08 against the Republic of Ireland - which they lost 1-0 - and San Marino - during which both Giggs and Bale scored in a 3-0 win.

Bale may not have played that often with his idol, but the Manchester United legend's career speaks for itself. He won the UEFA Champions League twice and the Premier League 13 times with United, with a UEFA Super Cup and Club World Cup and four FA Cups and four League Cups thrown in there as well, making him one of the most decorated players in football history.

The admiration between the pair was mutual and when Giggs was Bale's manager in the Wales national team, he said: "To win four, to go to Real Madrid, and be so successful, he's got to be [the best].

"He's the greatest I've seen. Obviously I didn't see John Charles play and many others around that time but he's the greatest I've seen.

"Great players turn up at the right moments and make the difference, and he's done it twice now in Champions League finals.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three days after tearing up as he announced his departure from the U.S.
  • In a recent development, after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • According to recent reports, "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three days after tearing up as he announced his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino mentioned he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

In a recent development, after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

According to recent reports, "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that notes it's not notable tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Sources indicate that pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his plans for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

It has been revealed that "What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino said. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

For perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an vital new chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

As for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his newly introduced role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

In a recent development, two years removed from starting a new job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-crucial clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

"For me, it's not difficult," he stated of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most vital [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Long chains of sugars known as polysaccharides support many biological functions, from strengthening tissues to modulating cell signalling. Synthesizing these compounds in the laboratory with precise lengths and architectures, which are needed to establish how the structures of polysaccharides affect biological behaviour, has been difficult. Writing in Nature, Yin et al.1 now report an enzyme-based strategy that produces highly uniform polysaccharides and enables chains to restart growth after consuming all of the sugar building blocks in the reaction, once more sugars are added. The authors achieved this control by adjusting how readily an enzyme binds the small sugar molecules that are used to initiate the growth of each chain.

Conceição has been out for around 40 days with a left shoulder problem, but is fit again and is expected to start on the right against Omonia in the Europa League tonight. Kick-off at the Allianz Stadium is at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT]. You can follow all the action, as it happens, on our Live Blog.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks. Things have changed since then, with numerous keepers coming through the ranks over the years, with most playing domestically or sitting on the bench for stronger European sides. However, that could be coming to an end for the team.

It has been revealed that during Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake. Kochen, who is playing his first season of first-team soccer at Lyngby in Denmark (where center back Neil Pierre also got his first taste of senior soccer), got the clean sheet against Mexico during that camp and turned that into a start against Haiti in Concacaf Nations League play in his native Miami, setting the USMNT up well to advance to the semifinals of the tournament.

Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be notable for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.

In a recent development, "I feel like I've grown quite a lot," Kochen said following the match, reflecting on his adjustment to the national team. "I'm getting used to competing at the international level, but I've just got to give it to my team because they've been unbelievable. They make it so easy to just come out here and play free and be me, so without them, this wouldn't be possible.".

Recent findings suggest that his growth is evident; one of the first things that comes to mind when watching the 20-year-old is his poise. Kochen had the ball at his feet plenty, completing all 20 of his passes to help send the attack on its way, and also made the two saves that he needed to on a mostly quiet night. His age also showed when Haiti scored with him out of position, a goal that was called back for offside, but you take the good with the bad for young players because that's a learning moment, and as he earns more reps at the senior level, those are the kind of mistakes that can be ironed out.

"I'm not saying he hasn't played games in Barcelona, but at the senior level, every game he plays, he gets better and better and better," one of Kochen's coaches, Andreas Bjelland, told CBS Sports. "Because understanding the full-pitch play, and not only being on the line, just taking shots, and being a training goalie, but now he's playing for points every week. He's growing as a player, as a person, and as somebody we can trust more and more in the stuff we do. So it's nice to see that it has come to this ... It's quite impressive.".

You can't teach poise, and spending more than five years in the Barcelona system reveals in how Kochen carries himself. It's becoming more common in American soccer for young players to test themselves abroad or to get into Major League Soccer teams at a younger age, and when they succeed, it goes a long way developmentally, as Kochen's case shows.

"He is a person who trusts himself a lot. That's also why he's a good goalie, that at such a young age he hasn't that big of a doubt of himself," Mikkel Jespersen, Lyngby's other coach said. "He knows what he's capable of doing, and that's really key as a goalie: that you trust yourself and know what things you are doing is something that can succeed in a longer period.".

Industry observers note that while it's unknown what the next USMNT manager will value in a keeper, being able to perform in an uncertain environment with your coach having one foot out the door is something that will go a long way for Kochen's chances. In keeper terms, Kochen has plenty of time ahead of him, as players at his position regularly play until their late 30s or early 40s, so if he can continue this trajectory, the question of who protects the net could be solved for the foreseeable future.

Recent findings suggest that of course, that's a lot of projecting, but when the next generation of the USMNT is developing at an astounding rate, it's only natural to think about where players like Kochen could end up. Doing this in only his first season of professional soccer is already impressive, but the best is yet to come.

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 18:33 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:51 EST, 26 November 2026.

Footage appears to show Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf that led to his fortunate second goal against Sporting Lisbon.

The Manchester United captain scored a bizarre goal against his former side on Wednesday night, with his long-range shot taking a fortuitous bobble off the Estadio Jose Alvalade pitch to leave goalkeeper Kaique Pereira helpless.

While fingers were initially pointed at the ground staff, footage shows the divot was actually created by Fernandes himself when he planted his boot into the turf while pressing high up the pitch moments earlier.

Reminiscent of former Liverpool forward Stan Collymore's famous bobbling goal past Blackburn Rovers goalkeeper Tim Flowers in 1996, Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

The goal summed up another chaotic evening for United, in which goalkeeping calamities, controversial refereeing calls, three penalties and a red card resulted in a 2-2 draw and left them 19th in the Champions League standings.

United trailed at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens saved one penalty before conceding another 75 seconds later that was converted by Luis Suarez after the Belgian's reckless challenge on Max Araujo.

Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

The visitors were left furious when Amad Diallo saw a first-half leveller ruled out after referee Szymon Marciniak blew his whistle too early for VAR to intervene, but United turned the game around shortly after the restart.

Lisandro Martinez, who had given away the first penalty, won one at the other end that Fernandes converted before the former Sporting star fired in the long-range effort that bounced over Pereira and into the net.

More drama followed as Lammens flapped at a cross under pressure from Suarez, allowing the striker to score, before Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have put undue pressure on Pereira when forcing an own goal from the goalkeeper.

United were left frustrated by what they viewed as a lack of consistency after Marciniak was sent to the pitchside monitor to review the second decision, and their mood darkened further when Youri Tielemans was sent off for a second booking late on.

Former United player Ashley Young claimed that 2022 World Cup referee Marciniak's decision-making during the clash was a 'disgrace'.

Young told BBC Radio 5 Live: 'The referee’s performance was just simply wow. The decisions that he gave.

'Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal.

'The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

'His decision-making is nothing more than a disgrace.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

Roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

And then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

Sources indicate that united fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

And yet by the 86th minute Matheus Cunha’s wild celebrations were encapsulating a wild night, the Brazilian ripping off his shirt after his dramatic winner before launching himself into a delirious crowd drunk on the euphoria of a victory that had seemed improbable in the extreme at the interval, when boos cascaded from the stands.

Sources indicate that whether this proves little more than a thrilling, heroic interlude in the endgame for Carrick, or the start of a genuine turnaround, is hard to know. And, let’s be clear, there was so much about the first-half performance to concern the hierarchy, who came under persistent, furious attack from fans at war with an ownership it reviles and wants gone.

But the second half stood firmly at odds with the shambolic display that had preceded it and suggested all may not be quite lost just yet.

Aston Villa visit Old Trafford on Sunday in the final game before the international break and, if Carrick can follow this with another win, then it will be intriguing to see where the Old Trafford board goes from there.

Speaking after the match, Michael Carrick was very positive about his side’s performance.

“It was a good night. I have to a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it and to the supporters. This place does incredible, magical things,” mentioned Carrick.

Recent findings suggest that “I thought we grew into it the first half  after giving the goals too easily. We spoke at half time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment and it certainly did that and the boys made the most of every opportunity and were fantastic in the end.”.

According to recent reports, asked about how he inspired the team at half-time he kept it simple: “Just not to get too disappointed about things. I thought we were coming into the game, getting around their box and it didn’t feel that way to the players because they were carrying too much frustration and disappointment and I knew we were doing some good things in the game against a really good team.

“Playing against man-to-man as much as they are, you probably get more failure than success and it’s still being positive and the boys responded so well to that.”.

As for whether this will change United’s momentum now, he was cautious not to get carried away.

It has been revealed that “Listen it’s one game. It depends on what happens next and we’ve got to capitalise on that but tonight the boys indicated an awful lot,” he said.

“And I thought we came out the second half, unfortunately with Carlos having to go off and Youri coming on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic, he showed everything that he is as a personality, as a character and with his experience to step in the game like that, and the boys just went with the flow and you could feel how positive it was and it was nice to see this place like that again.”.

Captain Bruno Fernandes also spoke after the match, acknowledging the difficulties the team has faced.

“It’s tough to say something at the moment to be honest. It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to play in the way we want, get the results we want. We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a whole game to get results and it’s been tough.

“But today was important to get a win. We knew after that we still had the fans with us, we felt we could change it with a goal and something and fortunately we did it today.”.

As for his penalty miss and re-take: “First one didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong but I got a second chance and I cleared my head and my mind was only on to get the ball in back of the net.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s been tough for the fans, we understand that. Having that belief from their side helps the team a lot and today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive.”.

After his first start as he returns from injury, Kobbie Mainoo was full of praise for the fans, saying he cherished the relationship the team had with them.

“It’s unlike anything else. We’d do anything for these fans on the pitch, all the love they give us throughout the season it’s only right we repay them and it’s a bit of fun just jumping into the stands with them.”.

Speaking to Amazon after the match, Youri Tielemans stated: “There has been a lot of pressure on him [Carrick] and that’s how we repay him, with a comeback like this, substantial character, big fight.”.

In a recent development, “We just kept working, we kept believing. We were on the front foot in the second half, we tried to push them into their goal and we succeeded.”.

It has been revealed that as for whether or not the performance would be enough to keep Carrick in his role at United: “That’s a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.

“At the end of the day we are on the pitch and we need to show what we are capable of and tonight, especially in the second half, we highlighted what we can do and we turned up the gears.

“Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and let’s hope we can build on this.”.

Manchester United fans are planning a series of in-stadium demonstrations at Old Trafford tonight in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s ownership.

Thousands of green and gold balloons – a nod to the club’s original colours as Newton Heath – are set to be released from the Stretford End when the Champions League music plays out ahead of kick-off.

There had been plans to bring a banner into the stadium bearing the words: “No new stadium, we want new owners” but that was blocked, apparently on the grounds of Uefa’s inability to sanction it in time.

The Glazers and Ratcliffe have come under growing attack this season with the club’s regular match going supporters at war with the owners.

A separate fans’ group has also been encouraging fans to join in anti Glazers and Ratcliffe chants in the 21st minute or, more specifically, after 20 minutes and 5 seconds: 20.05 is a nod to 2005, the year the Glazers completed their hostile takeover at Old Trafford.

The main surprise for Roma is in goal, as with first-choice keeper Svilar out already, it has been confirmed that backup keeper Pierluigi Gollini has injured his back today. He has been replaced by Colombian Devis Vásquez in goal.

Roma: Vásquez; Balerdi, Mancini, Hermoso; Rensch, de Roon, Mora, Wesley; Soulé, Cristante; Malen.

We have confirmation, Martínez is on the bench. He is replaced by Ayden Heaven while Bruno Fernandes is still with the captain’s armband in midfield. Kobbie Mainoo gets the nod as he returns from injury, along with Mateus Cunha and Mason Mount.

Lisandro Martínez has been dropped by Michael Carrick in the wake of his red card madness against Chelsea.

The United manager has opted to pair Ayden Heaven in central defence with Harry Maguire for the Roma game with Martinez dropping to the bench.

The Argentina defender received a second yellow card for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face in Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea when he was also culpable for the first goal.

Martinez has been in dire form this season and was fined and publicly apologised after publicly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and the Old Trafford board in the wake of the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Kobbie Mainoo returns to midfield after missing the last four games through injury.

Ayden Heaven has just come out to speak with Prime Video, which has led Gabby Logan to assume that means that Lisandro Martínez will not start for Michael Carrick tonight.

Speaking with her, former United legend Wayne Rooney has mentioned the Argentine has “simply not been good enough” and should not necessarily feature again under Carrick.

When Alan Shearer was asked if he would include Martínez on a team sheet tonight, he did not mince his words, calling him a “liability”.

Ahead of the confirmed line-ups coming out shortly, there are certain players we know we will not be seeing today.

Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Benjamin Sesko (shin) remain sidelined for United, while Marcus Rashford and Amad Diallo will be assessed before the match.

There are no latest concerns for Gasperini after his side’s latest match, the 5-2 win over Udinese, but he remains unable to select Muhammed Bah (ACL), Paulo Dybala, Manu Kone (thigh), Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) and first-choice keeper Mile Svilar (stress fracture, foot).

Happy Tuesday and thanks for tuning in to tonight’s coverage of Manchester United against Roma.

It has been revealed that it’s matchday four of the Champions League and Michael Carrick’s side host their Serie A opponents having failed to win any of their last nine matches across all competitions. Since their win against Sabah back in September (must feel like years ago to Carrick), they have suffered chastening defeats in Europe to Atlético Madrid and then Cesc Fabregas’s Como. This has been coupled with dismal performances in the Premier League, most recently a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea, where Lisandro Martínez was sent off for two ridiculous fouls.

Industry observers note that all in all, there is the feeling that Carrick is simply a dead man walking, limping towards the international break after the United hierarchy decided on a stay of execution in their crisis talks earlier this month. Despite the doom-mongering that circles the club, Carrick maintains that he has buried the hatchet with Bruno Fernandes following his captain’s public criticisms of the club, insisting that “the dressing room is a good place” in his pre-match press conference (more on that to come).

In a recent development, the visitors on the other hand, managed by Gian Piero Gasperini – who replaced Claudio Ranieri last summer – are certainly having a better time of it. They are currently unbeaten in Serie A with seven wins and three draws. They sit third and are the highest scoring side, with 28 goals from their 10 games. Free-flowing though their attack is, there a certainly defensive frailties there to exploit as they conceded three in a six-goal thriller against Napoli, as well as two in both matches against Cagliari and Udinese.

It has been 19 years since Carrick was part of a United side that thrashed Roma 7-1 at Old Trafford, with the midfielder scoring two. Tonight he faces that same opponent with his job hanging by a thread and it remains to be seen if his team can produce any semblance of that spark to turn the tide. Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1107 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.
  • More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.
  • Sources indicate that in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.

More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.

Sources indicate that in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost. And since 1990, nearly 490 million hectares of forest have been wiped out.

In a recent development, more recently, the trend has shifted in the opposite direction. Deforestation in the Amazon region of Brazil decreased by 41% from August 2025 through 2026 to reach its lowest rate since records began.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

To ensure lasting protection, the Tropical Forest Forever Facility was debuted in 2025 at the COP30 climate conference in Belem, Brazil.

Because rainforests are so vital for the world, the idea behind the fund was to give money to the countries where they are located to help them preserve and protect these ecosystems.

So far, these countries have made more profit through deforestation — for example, by mining natural resources on rainforest land or farming the area.

Starting in 2027, the TFFF is expected to generate the funds needed for rainforest conservation, in part via contributions from various countries. By the end of this year, a total of $10 billion (€8.9 billion) in government capital is due to flow into the fund, mainly in the form of low-interest loans.

In addition, the TFFF is expected to problem bonds to private investors, such as banks and investment firms, to raise additional funds — initially totaling about $40 billion.

In a recent development, going forward, the plan is for governments to contribute a total of $25 billion to the pot, and for private donors to contribute $100 billion. The fund will then invest this money in international financial markets with the aim of generating profits.

Private investors who purchase TFFF bonds can expect to earn about 5% interest per bond per year, said Felix Finkbeiner, the founder of the German environmental organization Plant-for-the-Planet, where he is responsible for forest conservation and advocacy.

"Private investors' capital is very well protected," Finkbeiner said, adding that any losses the TFFF might incur on the capital markets — for example, if the price of its bonds should fall — would be offset by government funds.

About 2.7% of the TFFF's profits would be set aside for countries with tropical forests.

Sources indicate that countries would receive $4 per year for every hectare of forest that they preserve instead of chopping down. At least 20% of these funds must be allocated to Indigenous peoples and local communities.

According to calculations by the TFFF Watch website, an independent platform launched by Plant-for-the-Planet to track investments, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for example, would receive about $333 million for its 2024 forest stock under this system.

Industry observers note that finkbeiner stated the subsidies would be paid only for intact ecosystems and not for timber plantations, with forest areas and their condition mapped and assessed using satellite imagery. Though it can sometimes be difficult to identify plantations accurately on satellite photos, he said, the technology has improved significantly over the last decade.

That means any NGO or external party with access to the satellite data can check the condition of the region, providing further oversight. If forest areas are cleared or damaged, money is deducted from the total.

Another safeguard: If countries don't use the TFFF funds for rainforest conservation, their payments could be frozen for the next few years.

Sources indicate that the TFFF is supposed to invest, whenever possible, in government bonds issued by emerging and developing countries. Above all, the idea is not to invest in projects that harm the climate — such as those linked to oil, gas, or coal investments.

The TFFF concept has received plenty of support from environmental organizations, in part because it gives countries in the Global South significantly more sovereignty than traditional forms of development financing.

"For example, if the government of Ghana wants to protect its rainforest today, it usually asks the World Bank for financial assistance — and then the World Bank in [Washington] DC decides whether Ghana is allowed to do so," Finkbeiner noted.

Industry observers note that the TFFF fund is also designed to be immune to donor countries' backing out in the event of a change in government, for example. Once a contribution is made, the money remains in the fund for 40 years before being paid back.

According to recent reports, continuing protection is also an incentive for countries receiving money from the fund. "When a upcoming government comes into power that wants to cut back a little on climate protection, they will realize: We'll get more money if we protect the rainforest," said Finkbeiner.

In a recent development, for the rainforest fund to actually get off the ground, a total of $10 billion in seed capital must be raised by the end of 2026. So far, the confirmed pledges from countries, NGOs and foundations total only $7.9 billion.

Eight countries have expressed a willingness to contribute so far, including Brazil, Indonesia, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

Industry observers note that norway, with a pledge of $3 billion, is the largest would-be donor. However, the government in Oslo is willing to honor its commitment only if the agreed-upon total amount is in place by the end of the year.

"This deadline isn't set in stone, but otherwise the Norwegian government will have real trouble getting it through parliament," Finkbeiner said.

According to recent reports, germany's commitment must also still be approved by the parliament. The German government has pledged about €1 billion to the TFFF starting in 2027, to be paid out over 10 years.

Other countries are also considering investing in the TFFF, including Canada, China, South Korea and the United Arab Emirates.

Industry observers note that philanthropic organizations have pledged $88 million to the fund so far, including $73 million announced this week during the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. Finkbeiner remains upbeat.

Industry observers note that "Promises like that always come at the last minute," he remarked. "I'm very optimistic that we'll secure more commitments at the COP — and in the course of December — and that we'll then reach that $10 billion.".

Mauricio Pochettino ordered Manchester United’s non-starters to complete an extra pitchside weights session immediately after the full-time whistle following Wednesday night’s dramatic 2–2 UEFA Champions League draw against Sporting CP.

The Argentine manager is renowned for his demanding approach to physical conditioning, and there were already signs of his methods being implemented following the full-time whistle in Lisbon.

Several of United’s non-starters were spotted taking part in an additional weights session on the pitch at the Estádio José Alvalade immediately after the game.

Among those involved were Matthijs de Ligt, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Andrey Santos, with the players using dumbbells and other conditioning equipment.

BBC Sports Live: “Some of Manchester United’s non-starters were out on the pitch doing a weights session after tonight’s game. Mauricio Pochettino must feel that fitness has an important part to play if performances are to improve.”.

Despite suffering a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first game in charge on Sunday, there were considerably more encouraging signs from United against Sporting.

The Red Devils looked sharper going forward, particularly after the interval, when Pochettino reportedly demanded greater aggression and more forward runs from his players.

Bruno Fernandes responded by scoring twice in the space of three minutes against his former club.

The Portuguese international converted a 48th-minute penalty before producing a delightful lob over Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira in the 50th minute to turn the game on its head.

United’s attacking movement and willingness to commit players forward offered an encouraging glimpse of what Pochettino could bring to the team with more time on the training ground.

Ultimately, United were left wondering how they did not leave Portugal with all three points.

After Senne Lammens spilled a routine 80th-minute cross to gift Luis Suárez a second equaliser, United thought they had snatched an 83rd-minute winner when Kaique Pereira flapped Fernandes’ corner into his own net, only for VAR to controversially rule it out for a soft foul by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper.

Combined with Youri Tielemans’ harsh stoppage-time second yellow card, Pochettino’s side were deeply unfortunate not to celebrate their first victory of the newly introduced era.

In a recent development, marcus is a sports journalist with more than five years of experience, specializing in Football, Formula 1 and Tennis. He was a football network writer for Reach PLC, writing for pages such as the Manchester Evening News, Liverpool Echo and Football.London.

From 2022 to 2026, Marcus worked for SPORTbible, playing a role in growing the brand’s F1 output and audience, as well as covering a wide range of sports including boxing, MMA, darts and athletics.

So far in his career, Marcus has interviewed some of the biggest names in different sports, including the likes of Max Verstappen, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ashley Cole, Jenson Button, Fred Vasseur and Tim Henman.

Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jonsson, who was in the famous Euro 2016 squad, has passed away at the age of just 37.

Back in the summer of 2016, Iceland surprised the football world as they managed to reach the quarter-finals of Euro 2016, which was held in France.

In the round of 16, Iceland were up against an England team packed with quality players, but pulled off a famous 2-1 win, with Ragnar Sigurdsson and Kolbeinn Sigthorsson scoring to cancel out Wayne Rooney’s opener.

Recent findings suggest that at the time, Jonsson was an unused substitute as Iceland were eventually knocked out 5-2 by France, who then fell to a 1-0 defeat in the final against Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal. During the tournament, Iceland were also remembered for their fans' spectacular thunder clap celebration at the end of matches.

According to The Sun, Jonsson was diagnosed with cancer earlier in the year and sadly lost the battle this week, leaving behind his wife and three children.

On Thursday evening, Jonsson’s club, Vikingur Reykjavik, confirmed the 37-year-old’s death in a statement.

“It is with great sadness and deep sorrow that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jonsson, Víkingur’s goalkeeper, passed away on Wednesday, November 25, surrounded by his loved ones.

“The thoughts of the club and all Víkingur are with his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences.”.

Born in Keflavik, Jonsson began his football career at Njarovík, a club based in the Reykjanesbaer region of Iceland.

In 2011, Jonsson signed for Stjarnan, going on to win the Icelandic title for the first time in the club’s history; they did so by going the entire season without tasting defeat.

During what was a brilliant title-winning season in 2014, Jonsson played a huge role and was eventually voted as the Players’ Player of the Year.

As a result of his domestic success, Jonsson has also played in the Europa League and the Europa Conference League, with Stjarnan beating the likes of Motherwell and Lech Poznan before losing to Inter Milan in 2014.

After leaving Stjarnan ahead of the 2015-2016 campaign, he went on to play for IK Start, Sandnes Ulf, Sandefjord and Viborg before rounding off his career at Vikingur Reykjavik.

According to recent reports, on the international stage, Jonsson earned eight caps for Iceland, having previously played for the U19s and the U21s. His senior team debut came in November 2014, when he replaced Ogmundur Kristinsson against Belgium.

  • Olympiacos were still unbeaten with three wins and a draw, but missed Leon Bailey, Chiquinho, Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, plus long-term absentees and cup-tied Yusuf Yazici, Balsa Popovic, Ayoub El Kaabi, Marius Mouandilmadji, Clayton, Joel Roca and Lorenzo Scipioni.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Omari Hutchinson kept Milan’s Europa League hopes alive by inspiring the 4-2 comeback win away to Olympiacos with a goal and two assists for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic, then Diego Moreira late on.

The Rossoneri had a terrible record in the Europa League, losing three of their four matches without finding the net, with a 4-0 victory away to RB Salzburg the outlier. They made the trip to Greece without Luka Modric, Francesco Camarda, Davide Bartesaghi, Strahinja Pavlovic, Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano, so squad rotation was kept to a minimum.

Olympiacos were still unbeaten with three wins and a draw, but missed Leon Bailey, Chiquinho, Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, plus long-term absentees and cup-tied Yusuf Yazici, Balsa Popovic, Ayoub El Kaabi, Marius Mouandilmadji, Clayton, Joel Roca and Lorenzo Scipioni.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Diego Moreira was valuable in defence during the opening minutes when charging down the Martins effort after a Panagiotis Retsos cross from the right.

Gelson Martins had a couple of pops from distance, but the first real chance was on 22 minutes with a curler that Maignan flew to palm around the upright.

Industry observers note that olympiacos were increasing the pressure and broke the deadlock with former Inter defender and Italy Under-21 international Pirola’s header, in off the underside of the crossbar from a Gustavo Sa corner. UEFA credited it as a Maignan own goal because the ball hadn’t completely crossed the line until it hit the goalkeeper on the way off the bar.

Pirola was every bit as decisive four minutes later, because Alphadjo Cisse had sprinted away on the counter, was tackled by the on-rushing goalkeeper, but still managed to prod it towards the empty net, only for the Italian defender to rush back for a desperate goal-line clearance.

It should’ve been 2-0 in added time, as Bruno Onyemaechi pulled back from the left for Pirola to fire over undisturbed from 10 yards.

It has been revealed that milan introduced Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah for the restart, but instead went 2-0 down. Maignan made the save on the Joao Silva angled drive, but as the move continued, the same player ran onto the Freuler through ball to blast into the roof of the net from just inside the area.

Just as Olympiacos were pouring forward for a third, they were caught by a rapid counter-attack. Hutchinson started the move from inside his own half, rode two tackles and cut inside to drill low into the far bottom corner to give Milan some hope.

Hutchinson contributed to the equaliser too as the comeback was completed, his cross from the right finding Cisse to squirm away from his marker to nod in at the back post.

Recent findings suggest that hutchinson was simply unstoppable in the second half when used out wide on the right, and he provided his second assist to turn the game around, met by the fantastic Pulisic volley from 12 yards with the right boot. It was the American’s fifth goal in his last six appearances.

Incredible work from Omari Hutchinson, who sets up Christian Pulisic for a fine volley 👌.

📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/eNxR1252Q6.

— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 26, 2026.

Cisse’s acrobatic bicycle kick didn’t quite come off from yet another Hutchinson cross, while Pirola’s risky interception prevented Adrien Rabiot meeting the Moreira assist.

In the final minute, penalty appeals were rejected because a header was charged down by Fikayo Tomori’s shoulder, but then Milan wasted the chance to add a fourth on the counter with Pulisic ballooning over.

With the last kick of the game, Hutchinson broke away on the counter from an Olympiacos corner, sent Pulisic down the left, he rolled across for Moreira to take a touch, then sweep in from 12 yards for 4-2.

The Rossoneri had never been able to beat a Greek team away from home before, managing only four draws and two defeats, including a 3-1 loss to Olympiacos in December 2018.

Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a bicycle-kick goal to kick things off, which was the emphatic send-off that was needed prior to Pochettino arriving in Manchester, but the USMNT were able to keep things up in the celebration in Cincinnati.

CHRISTIAN PULISIC GET ON YOUR BIKE‼️#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/Yb3yqXfC33.

In a recent development, julian Hall followed with a poacher's goal as Weston McKennie played orchestrator, and it continued a theme that whoever ends up taking over the national team will have tough decisions ahead. Folarin Balogun is struggling for minutes with Monaco and is looking to make a move at the end of the season, and Hall has done everything that he can to increase his own standing with five goals in six games for the USMNT.

Sources indicate that the Fresh York Red Bulls star has a ways to go considering that he's still only 18 and will need to gain experience against top teams in the world instead of just Haiti, but he also can't ask for a better start than what he has gotten off to. It's why this is such an attractive job for whoever takes over the USMNT. They'll be able to build upon the good that Pochettino has instilled; the talent is there to move the squad forward, and there's plenty to love about the youth of the USMNT.

Recent findings suggest that and alongside that, Pulisic has essentially screamed don't forget about me. During this camp, the Milan man has followed up on signing a new contract with the club by reaching 35 national team goals, moving into fourth all time for the USMNT over Eric Wynalda. Diego Kochen added to the good vibes with a third straight clean sheet, and Neil Pierre was even able to be cap-tied against the nation that he's also eligible for as the full-circle moments were left and right.

Pulisic, the former 17-year-old phenom, was subbed off for Cavan Sullivan, the current 17-year-old phenom, and while the goal difference may have been larger in the first leg between these sides, this felt like a more measured performance despite the strangeness of Pochettino's assistants heading to United while he managed the squad prior to catching his own charter.

In a recent development, this camp had every chance of being a disaster given the circumstances of Pochettino leaving, but all parties did what was needed during this camp. All dual nationals were capped, including Santiago Castaneda, showing that even on his way out, Pochettino made sure to take care of the future of the federation. On to the next round of the Concacaf Nations League with a upcoming manager and no complaints with the performance so far for the squad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are showing an interest in signing Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo, according to Sport Witness.

United's priority position to strengthen in the coming months is likely to be their defence, particularly, given the number of goals they've conceded so far this season.

It's been a disastrous campaign for United so far, as they sit in the relegation zone in the Premier League table in 19th position.

The Red Devils have won just one game in the league this season, fewer than every other side.

United have also struggled in the Champions League, particularly defensively, conceding 10 goals in five games.

The defensive options have been horribly exposed this season, and sorting that out is likely to be a main aim for Mauricio Pochettino.

Whether he can do that without making a large number of signings remains to be seen, so they may have to strengthen during the January transfer window.

According to a report from Sport Witness, one target could be Sporting CP left-back Araujo.

United have been following the Uruguayan international for many months now and, of course, saw him up close in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Araujo started in United's 2-2 draw with the Portuguese club, giving the Red Devils an opportunity to see him against United's forwards.

The report claims that Araujo has a £67 million release clause in his contract, but United could get him for less than that in January.

Araujo is also believed to be very open to making the move to Old Trafford, but it remains to be seen whether the Manchester club will make a play to secure his signature in January.

Activating Araujo's release clause certainly feels unlikely, given the price, but if they can negotiate a lower fee, it could be a smart signing.

Signing a left-back could be one of United's priorities heading into the January transfer window.

The Red Devils have many centre-backs on their books, even if a massive portion of them are failing to perform.

As a result, they might have to move some on before investing in new ones, but a left-back is a different story.

Luke Shaw has started to pick up injuries once again, which has been a huge problem throughout his career, so signing a long-term replacement would be a smart move.

Patrick Dorgu is another option at left-back, but he's often played further forward during his time at United.

The Manchester club have been forced to utilise the likes of Diogo Dalot at left-back in recent weeks, and it's clear that it's a position that needs strengthening.

Araujo could be the ideal player at the right price, given his age profile and attacking prowess.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.
  • Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (SIGNIFICANT) campaign called "The King's Return.".

BIG, a Christian group for footballers, has said it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

"Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he stated.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

In a recent development, "I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.".

He then stated that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

According to recent reports, in Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.

"We feel well prepared," Klopp remarked, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

It has been revealed that klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.

"We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 13:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 26 November 2026.

The SFA have been forced back to the drawing board for a second time in their efforts to introduce new proposals around youth development.

Led by chief football officer Craig Mulholland, the plans had been geared towards ensuring more Under-21 players in Scotland gain more minutes at first-team level.

The original intends were for two Scotland-eligible Under-21 players to start in domestic cup competitions, and for players to feature for a minimum of six per cent of all available minutes across a season in league campaigns.

When it became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t on board, a upcoming watered-down version was put back on the table.

But the newly introduced proposals have also now been met with resistance — forcing the SFA to kick the can further down the road into the new year.

There will now be no vote on the back of the upcoming AGM, with further discussions required prior to something more concrete coming to fruition for the start of next season.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has been sent back to the drawing board by clubs.

A statement from the governing body noted: ‘The Scottish FA has been encouraged by the productive dialogue with clubs regarding proposals to harness opportunities for young homegrown talent.

‘The most recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation in order to present a consolidated package of recommendations to an SPFL member vote.

‘The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews, when the reality of our domestic game’s standing in respect of playing time for under-21 players compared to the rest of Europe was made clear.

‘We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game.

‘It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams.

‘We have therefore agreed that the consultation process will continue into the Upcoming Year with the intention of a comprehensive proposal going to SPFL members within the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of William Hill SPFL season 2027-28.

‘The Scottish FA General Meeting to vote on the complementary Scottish Gas Men’s Scottish Cup proposals will now follow a similar timetable.

‘Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right.’.

Rare gene variants can affect a person’s height by up to 17 centimetres

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.
  • Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.
  • An analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.

Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.

An analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height. The work also uncovers previously unrecognized biological mechanisms that underly human growth.

The findings, published on 25 November in Nature1, might help with the development of treatments that mitigate height changes caused by some medical conditions, such as forms of dwarfism.

“The impact these genes have on any given individual can be massive in terms of accurately predicting their height or making sure they’re getting the right treatment for a disease,” states Adam Locke, a statistical geneticist at the Regeneron Genetics Center in Tarrytown, Fresh York.

About 80–90% of variation in adult height is caused by genetics. Projects analysing common gene variants have mapped thousands of DNA changes that can influence height. For example, a 2022 study identified more than 12,000 common genetic variants that collectively accounted for 40% of height variation in populations with European ancestry2.

However, how rare genetic variants (those found in less than 1% of a population) affect people’s height is less well studied.

To systematically probe how rare variants contribute to people’s stature, Locke and his colleagues gathered DNA and height data. In total, they looked at sequencing data from more than 1.4 million adults. They analysed the protein-coding sections of DNA and ran a series of tests to spot non-random links between height and both common and rare gene variants.

It has been revealed that the analysis uncovered rare variants in 207 genes, which, on average, were linked to a height difference of about two centimetres. The team also identified 17 genes that had a particularly strong effect on height. The variants associated with this gene set all resulted in the production of non-functional proteins. In the study, over 700 people had at least one of these loss-of-function variants.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

Industry observers note that individuals carrying such a variant were, on average, about nine centimetres taller or shorter than were people who didn’t have that variant. The strongest effects included a 17-centimetre reduction in height associated with a change to the ACAN gene and an 11-centimetre increase linked to the FBN1 gene. These effect sizes are more than 50 times larger than those of most genes commonly associated with height.

“We would expect rare genetic variants that disrupt gene function to have larger effects than common genetic variants, but the magnitude of some of these effects is particularly striking,” says Andrew Wood, a statistical geneticist at the University of Exeter, UK.

It certainly feels like it's time for Tottenham to move on from Richarlison.

Even just getting his wages off the books for the second half of the season would be beneficial, so Spurs need to find a way of getting rid of him in January.

A return to Everton could be a fairytale move for Richarlison, but it remains to be seen whether they can afford his wages or transfer fee.
