📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest roster of the year for the U.S. women's national team is here. Head coach Emma Hayes has named a 23-player roster for the upcoming 2026 Concacaf W Championship.

The tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play. Fans can watch all the Concacaf W Championship matches on Paramount+.

Recent findings suggest that in just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round. The U.S. and Canada earned direct byes into the tournament as Concacaf's top two ranked teams, and six teams now join them after a preliminary qualifying round. The USWNT will face El Salvador on Nov. 27 in the quarterfinal round, and if they advance, they'll clinch a spot in next year's World Cup. The other matchups are Canada against Panama, Mexico vs. Haiti, and Jamaica will play Costa Rica.

"It's been a great year of growth and learning for our team, and for a long time the focus has been on qualifying for the World Cup, so now that time has arrived," stated Hayes.

Sources indicate that "I want to see relentless consistency from our players, individually and as a team, and I want us to be elite in both penalty boxes. If we can achieve that, I'm confident those performances will carry us through to meet our standards and goals. This is my first Concacaf event and the first for many of our players, so we're all looking forward to the experience.".

Hayes selected a full roster that features several players competing in their first-ever senior-level World Cup qualifying tournament, and a handful of veterans. Just eight of the 23 players selected were members of the 2022 Concacaf W Championship roster: forwards Mallory Swanson, Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson, and Ashley Sanchez; defender Emily Fox; and midfielders Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle, and Sam Coffey -- who joined mid-tournament that year.

Industry observers note that coffey returns to the roster after missing two previous international windows while managing a lower-leg injury. Defender Naomi Girma is out as she continues to manage a lingering calf injury. The centerback has not featured with the national team since April, and has yet to play with Chelsea FC this season. Midfielder Olivia Moultrie is currently rehabbing from an ACL injury sustained in August. Other notable omissions on the roster are Jaedyn Shaw and Ally Sentnor, both of whom have been part of U23 and senior camps throughout the year.

This is just the third camp for the attacking line of "triple espresso" since the 2024 Olympics. If the trio starts a match during the Concacaf W Championship, it will be the first time they start a game together since the gold medal match. Both Swanson and Wilson have worked their way back into senior camps over the year following maternity leave.

Listed by position (club; caps/goals).

Goalkeepers (3): Claudia Dickey (Seattle Reign FC; 12/0), Mandy McGlynn (Utah Royals FC; 6/0), Phallon Tullis-Joyce (Manchester United, ENG; 8/0).

Defenders (8): Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC; 72/3), Kate Del Fava (Utah Royals FC; 1/0), Emily Fox (Arsenal FC, ENG; 80/1), Avery Patterson (Houston Dash; 15/1), Tara Rudd (Washington Spirit; 12/0), Evelyn Shores (Angel City FC; 0/0), Gisele Thompson (Angel City FC; 12/0), Kennedy Wesley (San Diego Wave FC; 9/1).

Midfielders (6): Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current; 7/1), Sam Coffey (Manchester City, ENG; 46/5), Lindsey Heaps (Denver Summit FC; 180/40), Claire Hutton (Bay FC; 22/1), Rose Lavelle (Gotham FC; 124/29), Lily Yohannes (OL Lyonnes, FRA; 22/1).

Forwards (6): Michelle Cooper (Kansas City Current; 16/1), Trinity Rodman (Washington Spirit; 59/13), Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage; 30/4), Mallory Swanson (Chicago Stars; 105/39), Alyssa Thompson (Chelsea FC, ENG; 34/4), Sophia Wilson (Portland Thorns FC; 65/25).

According to recent reports, ashley Sanchez's return to the roster comes after standout performances against Spain last window and a stellar 2026 NWSL regular season where she won the Golden Boot with 20 goals scored. She was also nominated for the 2026 NWSL MVP award. A positional shift to left winger and an outrageous amount of scoring have all led her back to the USWNT due to consistent performances, a key factor for Hayes with her large player pool.

"Be consistent first of all in performance. Ashley Sanchez wasn't on our radar, not because she isn't talented, but there were certain things we demanded from the performance that I think she has delivered in her game on a regular basis. So, I think that's the first thing. I think you've seen that includes Croix Bethune coming into this camp -- been outstanding in the number 10 position all year, and would have been in last camp as well if she was fit. You do have to consistently find consistent performances, particularly if you're a player that doesn't have credit in the bank," Hayes said.

As the World Cup gets nearer, finalizing a roster for the 2027 summer tournament is even closer. Things like consistent form and senior-level experience will come into play when naming a final 23 for the World Cup for Hayes.

"If you're a Mallory Swanson and delivered on a world stage on a regular basis for the national team, it does alter things slightly. No, we don't want players that are in our group that are in a place where they're not fighting to improve every day or be as competitive as they could possibly be, but I think when players have stacked and accumulated a lot of experience over a period of time, that is always going to put them in a steady position," Hayes explained.

"But it doesn't guarantee anything. I will be unafraid to leave anybody off that plane if I don't feel that they are applying themselves to put ourselves in the best possible position to compete. Which is why this upcoming camp, our job is to qualify for the World Cup, and so everything we have worked towards is ensuring that every player that comes in at camp makes sure they lift their level and they position the team to have the most positive outcome, regardless of the opponent. And I'd be demanding as much as I always do, but I have a substantial expectation from our senior players to step up.".

El Salvador is the eighth-ranked team in the Concacaf W Championship and earned its spot following a preliminary qualifying round. The group is coached by manager Eric Acuña, who recently made headlines for harshly criticizing his players in a press conference following losses to Paraguay last month.

Still, Hayes and the staff aren't taking any opponent lightly no matter the rankings or state of the locker room.

"It's a team that knows is competing for something, so it doesn't matter the opponent; they're competing to go to a World Cup, and do I think that will be it will be demanding and taxing? And yes, I do. In many different ways, because the expectations are all on us. I think for them, it's how are they going to disrupt us and make it difficult? But they have two players in the front line that can cause a lot of problems, particularly in transition. So we have to set up for that," Hayes stated.

"I think when it when it comes to the players, I've always championed creating positive environments for players. And yeah, I'm sad for the players to hear what they've gone through, but as always, I can't control that. I want the best for players all of the time in their environments, but I am here to represent the U.S. and try and help us qualify for the World Cup. So my focus is on that. Even if my heart goes out to the players and I think we still have a lot of work to do in the women's game to keep driving female-centered, female-lens environments where women can thrive.".

Liverpool have received a potentially significant injury boost after initial medical tests suggested Víctor Munoz has avoided a serious knee injury following Wednesday night’s 3-0 Champions League victory over Club Brugge.

Fears of a lengthy layoff initially surged at the Jan Breydelstadion when the 23-year-old collapsed in agony in the 42nd minute after colliding with Club Brugge defender Jorne Spileers following a blistering run into the penalty area.

Although a stretcher was called onto the pitch, Munoz was eventually able to limp off under his own power.

Sources indicate that according to Spanish outlet Marca (as relayed by Tribuna), initial medical tests conducted back on Merseyside suggest Munoz has escaped structural ligament damage. Instead, the setback is believed to be a heavy impact knock.

Final confirmation pending as Liverpool hope for best news.

While the early diagnostic feedback is hugely encouraging, final medical confirmation remains pending as club doctors continue monitoring how the joint responds once swelling subsides.

Even if it proves to be a severe bone bruise, Sunday’s Premier League Merseyside derby away against Everton may come slightly too soon.

Industry observers note that speaking during his post-match press conference in Belgium, head coach Andoni Iraola had already offered cautious optimism that the problem was not very serious. He noted (via Liverpoolfc.com):.

In a recent development, “He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished.

“It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it’s just this knock… After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.”.

Signed from Osasuna for £34.5 million during the summer transfer window, Munoz is rapidly looking like one of the bargains of the season.

Fresh off finding the net in Sunday’s 4-0 demolition of Manchester United, his electric pace, direct dribbling, and relentless pressing has been vital to Iraola’s attack.

Munoz has scored three and assisted another in five starts this season across all competitions.

While Bradley Barcola and Rio Ngumoha may be ahead of Munoz in the pecking order at the moment, Andoni Iraola is doing a wnoderful job managing the squad, rotating the players across the various competitions.

Liverpool will hope that Munoz’s injury isn’t too serious and that he is back soon ahead of the busy run of fixtures in the coming month.

The Premier League is here for 2026/27 and over £3 billion spent in the summer, there is more firepower than ever in the world's most watched league.

Years gone by have seen some of the craziest goal compilations for completed seasons and the 2026/27 campaign has already provided its share of action as fans continue to feast on an incredible lineup of players and moments.

According to recent reports, here, GIVEMESPORT is tracking the best goals as and when they hit the net, ranking them in order based on a number of factors, which you can see below — culminating in our goal of the season pick come May, with the best strikes worldwide tracked in our Puskas Award power rankings. Here's how it stands.

There's something about Cole Palmer and Brighton: he loves playing against the Seagulls. It might be because they play the type of free-flowing football that allows him to score solo efforts like this one in their 4-3 victory in the opening weeks of the new season.

Recent findings suggest that palmer picked up the ball deep in Brighton's half and eyed the space ahead to the left to drive into. He took a few defenders along for the ride, showing quality dribbling, close control and pace, before applying a classy, curled finish to settle the game. Classic Palmer.

Recent findings suggest that we've seen Bryan Mbeumo score plenty of clinical efforts during his time in the Premier League, and this opener against Everton reveals that he is still improving. The poise, the quality and the ruthlessness at which he netted this ensure it ranks high on the list.

After receiving the ball on the right wing, he opted to move inside, hurrying the Everton defenders and midfielders, driving into the open space and firing a powerful low strike that left Jordan Pickford, one of the league's best goalkeepers, stranded.

This list is great because it right now holds a lot of variety, and Nilson Angulo brings a quality free-kick to the table here. He joined Sunderland in February but not many people know of the young attacker.

That changed in an instant as he produced a stunning free-kick from distance that cannoned in against Ipswich Town. Unfortunately, it was in vain, as the home side grabbed a key victory. Yet, the strike remains beautiful and likely remain on this list until another set-piece goal can top it.

This is a stereotypical 'great' goal. Harvey Barnes has proven over the years that he can produce big moments and powerful strikes with either foot — but this strike against Bournemouth was one of his best.

Recent findings suggest that with a defender for tech giant on the left, he quickly squared him up, cut inside and then fired a curling strike that nestled just inside the post. Virtually unstoppable, it deserves plenty of credit.

In what was the first match since City's guilty verdict, the occasion of Liverpool vs Manchester City at Anfield took on a whole fresh atmosphere — but Enzo Maresca's side revelled in the jeers to sweep aside their rivals by a comfortable 3-0 scoreline.

Sources indicate that A red card for Ryan Gravenberch ensured City had the upper hand, and goals from Erling Haaland and Jérémy Doku had seen them take an unassailable lead. Then, City's wizard Rayan Cherki added the finishing touch with their third.

Recent findings suggest that cherki dummied Elliot Anderson's pass into the box, and then spun in behind to take the layoff from Joško Gvardiol. He controlled the ball, cut back inside to sell the defender before rolling it in with ease. Classy and brutal, all at once.

Following a corner that was cleared to the edge of the box, the former Nottingham Forest midfielder showcased an exceptional technique to control his powerful volley low and in, managing to avoid the crowd of players in the box, to bring his side level.

In a recent development, the Paraguayan attacker has been hailed for his technical brilliance, and briefly featured on this list due to an exceptional assist he managed for striker Emersonn in the early parts of the season. This time, it's all about Enciso himself.

Facing a difficult Hull City side away from home, Ipswich found themselves chasing the game, at 2-1 down. Enciso stepped up, beat two players, then shifted it onto his left and fired an incredible strike into the top corner with his weaker foot. He is certainly their main man and when it comes to fighting off relegation in the Premier League table, they'll need more quality like this from him.

Sources indicate that add this to the list of Premier League centre-backs who've fired in unstoppable efforts. However, whilst this did make it 2-1 at the time, they fell to a sorry 4-1 defeat.

In a recent development, still, Botman carried the ball deep in Coventry's half before firing his left-footed strike that arrowed into the near-post top corner. It's the type of strike that stands the test of time. Powerful, accurate and unforgettable.

Recent findings suggest that there seems to be a trend with the promoted sides this season: none of them are afraid to have a go from distance. If Coventry are to stay up, then goals from like from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto are exactly what they need to pull off an incredible escape from the drop.

Against Crystal Palace, and their latest boss Thomas Frank, the Japan international managed his second strike from outside of the box in as many weeks.

In what was first a tough cross to control, he chested it down and then fired it in from distance powerfully, leaving Dean Henderson with absolutely no chance.

Brighton has unearthed another gem in Diego Gomez. In an era where ball-striking from distance is less of a commonplace tactic, the young attacker is changing the status quo, as this strike marked his second entry on the list.

According to recent reports, facing another of the league's rising teams in Brentford, Gomez took it upon himself to settle a tight game, showcasing his quality with a fearsome weaker foot strike from outside the box. Something tells me he's going to feature on here again in the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to be the stuff of nightmares.

His record at Barcelona now reads 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.

It was Emery’s 55th birthday and with the Prince of Wales and Prince George both in attendance, Villa fans were hopeful of another memorable European night. But from the moment midfielder João Gomes handed Barcelona their opening goal, it was always going to be an uphill struggle.

Emery has suffered many uncomfortable occasions at this grand old stadium, none more so than the notorious “La Remontada” of 2017 when he last competed here in the Champions League with Paris St-Germain.

This latest visit would become his heaviest defeat in Europe as Villa manager. With three wins from the opening four matches, they still have a fine chance of progressing to the knockout stage. Yet, aside from the mistakes, there will be a sense that Villa could have capitalised more against a team in the midst of a defensive injury crisis. They did have a number of chances in the first half but were left to rue their lack of ruthlessness.

Aston Villa make a mistake at the back and Lamine Yamal makes them pay inside 10 minutes ⚡ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/1IcWOPMJlt.

Recent findings suggest that at the heart of Barcelona’s victory was Lamine Yamal, their outstanding jewel from the academy. The 19-year-old became the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history, eclipsing the record of 13 he previously shared with Kylian Mbappé, with the opening goal.

Yamal was orchestrating everything from the pace of the match to the volume of the supporters, at one point imploring them to raise the noise in the first half with both arms aloft.

There was also another impressive performance from England international Anthony Gordon and Raphinha, who dedicated his two goals to the memory of Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife forward, who died on Tuesday.

With that tragedy fresh in the minds and the Nou Camp under construction, it was a peculiar atmosphere at times.

According to recent reports, the defeat marked the end of Villa’s 100 per cent record in the competition, with a tough test away at Galatasaray up next before they host PSG in December. They remain high up in the table and have often displayed a propensity to bounce back quickly from defeats.

Sources indicate that emery said: “We are in a process and this was a very good test against a team like Barcelona. We are not at the level we want to achieve but there are a lot of experiences for us to take. Overall, we are competing fantastically in the Champions League and there is still work to do.

“Over the process we’ve had here, we have made mistakes but then overcame them. We accept this defeat but take a lot of information from it.”.

Nine years have passed since Emery’s last visit in this competition and time has not proved a great healer.

Recent findings suggest that then in charge of PSG, Emery witnessed his team surrender a 4-0 first-leg lead to lose 6-5 on aggregate. Any matches where he is involved at the Nou Camp will revive memories of that remarkable comeback. He must have feared a repeat of more pain when Yamal, making his 37th Champions League appearance, rewarded Barcelona’s early pressure.

Industry observers note that villa’s defending needed to be as close to perfect as possible, but they were exposed after a poor error of judgment from Gomes. Under pressure from Barcelona’s attackers, Gomes panicked and played a blind pass into the path of Yamal, who bent his left-footed shot into the corner.

That mistake could have threatened to damage confidence but Villa did respond. Matty Cash’s half-volley from inside the penalty area was only a few inches wide, while Johan Manzambi side-footed wide of the goal after a quick break down the right from Nicolas Jackson.

With Andreas Christensen, Eric García, Xavi Espart and Jules Koundé all absent here, Barcelona’s defence did appear vulnerable. Jackson was targeting the flanks and having his more dangerous moments challenging their high line. Emery paced his technical area, imploring his players to remain focused.

Industry observers note that yet Barcelona’s forward three were always a threat and they increased their lead eight minutes into the second half. Raphinha was given too much room to turn in the penalty area and his shot took a heavy deflection off the heel of Pau Torres to find the bottom corner. Emery was furious, appearing to raise his fist in the air at another poor goal conceded.

Raphinha doubles Barcelona's lead with his 18th goal of the season! 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/NzFPYVzDuj.

Barcelona added a third goal with Raphinha converting from close range after a sublime pass from João Cancelo.

Recent findings suggest that raphinha dedicated his goals to De Miguel, who died on Tuesday after sustaining serious injuries during a match the previous night. He noted: “Tonight I don’t want to talk about football. I want to send a lot of strength to Jesus de Miguel’s family.

“May he rest in peace. In the end, this can happen to anyone. The truth is that it’s very tough. When we saw the news this morning, it was complicated. I’m incredibly shocked and sad. In the end, you go to play a match, and the same thing could happen to you. From myself, from the club, we want to send a lot of strength to his family.”.

Villa did continue to fight for a consolation, with substitute Leon Goretzka heading against the post and their 3,000 travelling fans continued to sing in the rain after the final whistle.

This was the first encounter between the two clubs since the European Super Cup Final in January 1983, and yet another reminder of the upward trajectory under Emery.

Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have made the trip over to Spain to take on Barcelona in the Champions League on matchday four. These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

Aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

“In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery remarked. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

“[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

Barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick noted. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which revealed it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

#140246. Why U.S. Soccer's move to name Emma Hayes to the USMNT hiring committee makes sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1991 w)

Why U.S. Soccer's move to name Emma Hayes to the USMNT hiring committee makes sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1991 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.
  • Sources indicate that men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that WASHINGTON, D.C. – By the time U.S. Soccer confirmed Mauricio Pochettino's departure for Manchester United early Friday morning, the announcement itself was far from a surprise. The press release included the usual formalities – Steve Cherundolo, the U-23 U.S. men's national team head coach, would fill in for the Dec. 13 friendly against Jamaica that falls outside the FIFA international match calendar, and the assurance that the search for Pochettino's USMNT successor would begin shortly. Federation CEO J.T. Batson and COO Dan Helfrich will unsurprisingly lead the search, as will "the soccer leadership team at U.S. Soccer that includes" assistant sporting director Oguchi Onyewu. There was one unique detail tucked into the announcement, though.

Emma Hayes, the U.S. women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.

Sources indicate that men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event. They operate on different calendars and in the best case scenarios, each team has dedicated members of staff. Hayes' name-drop as news of Pochettino's exit became official, then, is a unicorn-like sighting, even if U.S. Soccer often champions a spirit of collaboration between all of its national teams. It is uncommon for the head coach of one senior national team to help recruit a counterpart but in U.S. Soccer's case, it makes complete sense.

Hayes' coaching career, which spans two decades and two continents, means her inclusion on the federation's soccer leadership team is an obvious one. She is amongst the most respected soccer minds in the game, which easily makes her one of the most crucial people on U.S. Soccer's payroll no matter how you look at it. That will be especially true in a hiring process that has to conclude with a compelling follow-up act to Pochettino's splashy arrival two years ago. Her perspective might actually be vital in the process, which only adds to the intrigue of what's next for the USMNT.

"We have an extraordinary gift, which is a women's national team manager who's incredibly insightful, bright mind about the sport, who has a set of personal experiences and relationships that span the club and international game, the men's and women's game, the domestic and international club game, and who also has lived in the shoes of what it's like to be a U.S. national team senior coach," Helfrich told CBS Sports on Thursday. "It is a no-brainer that that mind and that voice has a really prominent seat at the table when we're talking about notable moves for the federation.".

USMNT coaches are rarely style hires; look no further than the list of people to hold the job on a full-time basis this century and the picture paints itself. The only thing Bruce Arena, Bob Bradley, Jurgen Klinsmann, Gregg Berhalter and Pochettino seem to have in common, outside of the job they all once held, is that they were all tasked with some sort of cultural reset depending on the task at hand. That likely will not be the case for Pochettino's successor, though, who will inherit a team with a clear style of play, a healthy mix of veteran players and rising talents and plenty of time on the clock until the next World Cup. The job will be defined in part by continuity, even with the necessary allowance for the new hire to put their unique spin on things.

That's where Hayes' expertise should play a crucial role, and the same goes for Onyewu. Hayes' tactical know-how makes her as qualified as anyone employed by U.S. Soccer to establish the right stylistic profile for the next USMNT coach, especially with the spirit of continuity in mind. Pochettino's track record with the U.S. team was mixed but at its best, his high-intensity, attack-minded approach suited the player pool really well and continues to do so. Hayes, a tactical pragmatist who prioritized attack-minded teams herself with Chelsea and the USWNT, will be more than able to help match candidates to the player pool they will spend the next several years working with. Hayes admitted as much on Wednesday when addressing the topic for the first time.

According to recent reports, "I work really closely with J.T. in particular and even more so with Dan as we're growing to develop the American soccer movement and J.T. asked if I would be involved as a technical voice, to be involved with the process and I feel confident in the group of people that have been put together to create a thorough process to select the next men's national team coach," she stated. "My role is merely to support that through a technical lens, knowing I do this job, albeit with the women's team, and that I've coached for a number of years and can offer some of that insight into the application of what to look for and why and like I said, I feel confident in the group that are being put together. I think it'll be a very thorough process. I think that's the most important part of it and like I said, I feel very embedded in what we're doing with the federation so it doesn't feel unusual to me so, like I've said many times, let's build off the good work that Mauricio has done. I think that's the important part and let's get it right.".

That's especially true considering the fact that there are very few slam-dunk candidates to replace Pochettino. Pep Guardiola, months into a sabbatical after a decade with Manchester City, is an obvious target for U.S. Soccer but it is entirely unclear how interested he would be in the vacancy. If he's out of the running, the list of contenders with genuine international appeal dwindles quickly but it does not necessarily mean the list of worthy candidates vanishes with Guardiola. The hiring committee will need to be strategic in that case, both in terms of creating a list of contenders and then narrowing them down over the interview process, Hayes providing an important perspective along the way.

The jobs of the USMNT and the USWNT head coaches are hardly apples-to-apples but even then, one will still have an acute idea of what the other's job entails. There is inherent value in having a coach help in the process of hiring another coach, since they hold such singular positions – they are often treated as the be-all, end-all when it comes to their team's success, fairly or otherwise. She can also speak to the cadence of national teams, which varies greatly from the club game where coaches essentially work with their players every day during a long season.

According to recent reports, "Everyone is aware of the major differences between coaching at the club level and international level, and the main difference is just time on the field and time with your players," Hayes told CBS Sports earlier this year when asked about Pochettino. "Every international coach would love to have more time with their team, but that's not the nature of the international calendar and it's something I know we both had to get used to and are still getting used to … I said a few times that it's almost like we are grandparents. We get to see the players for a week or so and then we send them back to their parents, which is their clubs.".

Recent findings suggest that outside of her tactical expertise, though, Hayes represents U.S. Soccer's ambitious turn in recent years as much as Pochettino does. She was hired because of her reputation as a serial winner at Chelsea, where she won eight league titles and seven cups. She continued the trend in short order with the USWNT – two months after officially starting in the role, she won Olympic gold at the Paris Games in 2024. U.S. Soccer has equally ambitious goals for the men's team, though the timeline will understandably be longer for that program. They continue to target the USMNT's first World Cup quarterfinal appearance since 2002 but in between, they also hope to medal in the Olympics' men's soccer event, which is contested by U-23 teams, for the first time when the Games come to Los Angeles in 2028. More than many at the federation, Hayes has experience with the intangibles it takes to reach those heights and that's exactly why she was hired in the first place. It also reflects what U.S. Soccer's executives are looking for in the next USMNT head coach.

"The most key characteristic is someone with ambition that matches ours, which is high and so when you have, then, that high shared ambition, then you look for the experience, the talent, the understanding that accompanies that ambition," Helfrich noted.

Beyond that, though, Hayes in particular has an idea of what the USMNT job might entail. She is the best of both worlds – she began her coaching career in the U.S. two decades ago and has a deep understanding of the American soccer landscape, but made a name for herself in her native England and can also bring a useful outsider's perspective. There is no perfect equivalent to Hayes waiting for the USMNT job since no coach with experience in the American game has truly broken into the top tiers of the sport just yet, the federation likely to settle for one or the other. Hayes' understanding of both orbits, though, makes her an notable guiding force along the way. She might be the only qualified person to answer how much to weigh the insider's perspective with the accomplished outsider's point of view when looking for the next USMNT head coach, in large part because she is the only person who boasts an equal share of it.

According to recent reports, hayes' expertise alone means she will be as valuable a sounding board as any, to the point that it's hard to minimize her ability to offer input down to one or two straightforward things. There is one more thing Hayes might have that no one at U.S. Soccer does – easy access to some of the most notable coaches in the game.

In a recent development, over the course of her successful 12-year tenure at Chelsea, Hayes became one of the most respected coaches in England. She became the first woman to win the Football Writers Association's Tribute Award in 2024 shortly before leaving England for the U.S., and has earned the praise of many of her counterparts in the men's game along the way. Out of anyone at U.S. Soccer, Hayes might actually have the most compelling list of phone numbers in her contacts. She has said Sir Alex Ferguson, a coaching legend if there ever was one after his storied 27-year tenure at Manchester United, calls her "from time to time." Hayes has been in touch with a handful of her contemporaries over the years, including those who have been on U.S. Soccer's radar at one point or another. In her 2024 book, "A Completely Different Game," Hayes said she heard from Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp after having an emergency hysterectomy because of endometriosis in 2022. The pair "sent me long messages, expressing deeply felt emotions," as did Graham Potter and David Moyes.

The rolodex is a covetable one, if ex-U.S. Soccer sporting director Matt Crocker can serve as an example. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway. An awards show, countless events, and media days were all on the agenda ahead of Saturday's substantial game. That included the annual state of the league by commissioner Jessica Berman on Thursday.

Industry observers note that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m. ET. She also announced a few new league rules and future match events.

Here are the new things coming to NWSL:.

The commissioner introduced the new player development rule. While the league previously submitted paperwork for a potential future second=division league, conversation and planning around that is presently paused with the upcoming 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup and efforts to grow NWSL in other ways.

Recent findings suggest that "As we grow from 16 to 18 teams in 2028, we know that we have to prioritize the pipeline, not just the pipeline of players, but the pipeline of talent that supports the players in the daily training environment. One of the things that makes the United States so uniquely positioned in the global women's soccer landscape is the depth of that potential pipeline," stated Berman in her opening remarks.

It has been revealed that "That's why today we're announcing the NWSL Player Development Rule. It's an important step in strengthening the pathway to professional soccer for the next generation of players. The rule creates actual incentives for clubs to invest in identifying, developing, and retaining young talent, and it gives the clubs the flexibility to design their programs in the way that makes sense with their sporting philosophies.".

More information and the types of incentives will roll out for clubs as the new player development rule goes into effect, but it is another step in future roster-building for clubs now alongside general player signings, transfers, the High Impact Player rule, and the Under-18 mechanism.

The addition of the rule is paving the way for more support staff and systems in place. The commissioner also declared the fresh NWSL Sporting Executive Program, meant to provide more support for club leadership development. The inaugural set of leadership includes six executives from the league who will participate in the program.

Recent findings suggest that "Developing the future of the sport is not just limited to the players; it's also about the technical staff who surround those players each and every day ... this is a first-of-its-kind program invested in talent, and it was curated and developed in collaboration with U.S. Soccer and FIFA. This latest year-long initiative will provide sporting executives at our clubs with curated, specialized education, mentorship, and leadership development opportunities tailored around the unique demands of our league and the women's professional game," she said.

Recent findings suggest that the NWSL commissioner then announced the future site of the next NWSL Challenge Cup. The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup will take place in Austin, Texas, next summer.

In a recent development, the tournament has evolved since its first iteration as a placeholder for the COVID-19-affected season and is now a unique one-off marquee match between top clubs, typically the NWSL Shield titleholders and the NWSL Championship winners. In years where one club wins both, the game is a rematch of the previous NWSL Championship match.

"Following the success of this year's Challenge Cup in Columbus, where we took the event to a neutral site to give an opportunity to introduce the NWSL to a upcoming community," she remarked.

The 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup was between 2025 NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current and 2025 NWSL Championship winners Gotham FC. The 2026 competition was held in Columbus, Ohio. The state will now welcome its first NWSL franchise in 2028 alongside another expansion club in Atlanta.

It has been revealed that fans will undoubtedly make the connection and wonder if there is a future where an NWSL club calls Austin home. At the moment, there are three NWSL clubs in California and only one in Texas, the Houston Dash.

"We're really excited to create another special experience for our fans and our players while making the NWSL a place that can invite new audiences," Berman mentioned about heading to Austin.

Commissioner Berman celebrated the league's recent return to the nation's capital for another NWSL Championship. The city hosted the 2022 event and now returns four years later with more attention on the league, the clubs, and its players than ever before.

"Today, we're bigger, stronger, more visible, and more ambitious than ever before, and the next five years are going to redefine what's possible. We have an extraordinary opportunity in front of us, and we intend to seize it," she said.

In a recent development, two incoming clubs set for 2028 and new player roster rules are just the beginning of NWSL's next chapter. There's still the potential for more clubs on the horizon, and current clubs Houston Dash and Racing Louisville are in the process of vetting for a sale to new ownership as franchise entry fees into the league are booming to new heights.

And of course, there is still the biggest game of the year to play on Saturday.

Industry observers note that "The Washington Spirit are back in the championship for the third consecutive year, determined to bring home that title. And standing in their way is the Kansas City Current, with its own ambitions to win a championship after winning the Shield in 2025. These are two exceptional clubs, two incredibly passionate fan base, and the championship is still to be decided, [we're] very excited about the rest of this week.".

Wouter Vrancken claimed that Monaco’s 94th-minute winner at Tynecastle has not significantly diminished Hearts’ chances of reaching the knockout phase of the UEFA Conference League.

Vrancken’s team were left sickened when Folarin Balogun’s goal settled a thrilling contest in stoppage time to condemn them to a third consecutive defeat in the league phase of the competition after their away losses to Trabzonspor and Thun.

Hearts, who have just one point from their opening night draw at home to Nordsjaelland, now have to win both of their remaining games – at home to Bosnian side Borac on December 10 and away to Pafos in Cyprus a week later – to have any chance of further progress.

‘I don’t think losing that point makes a difference,’ insisted Vrancken. ‘The pleasing thing for me was that at 2-2 we still wanted to go and try to win the game.

In a recent development, ‘Three points would have made a difference — zero or one point tonight doesn’t make a difference towards the next two games. We have to win them both now, so that doesn’t change.’.

Vrancken took pride from Hearts’ display against their Ligue 1 opponents as two spectacular strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota cancelled out a Balogun penalty and Edan Diop’s goal in a breathless first half.

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken consoles goalscorer Sabah Kerjota as he is substituted.

While Balogun’s late winner was harsh on Hearts, Vrancken believes his players paid the price for poor game management and was critical of the contribution of subs Josh McPake, Finlay Pollock and James Wilson who came on in the closing stages of the game.

‘It did feel cruel but at the same time we have to learn from that situation,’ remarked Vrancken. ‘Until then, we were really solid in not giving chances away.

It has been revealed that ‘I expect more from the guys who came on. We can win the ball with fresh players or make a foul somewhere to keep the result. I expect that kind of battling for the team, so we can do better there.

‘But the biggest thing is the performance we put on the park tonight against a really good side, knowing that we still have nine injuries and still do that against them. I’m really proud of them.

In a recent development, ‘The goals we scored were really good and you see the confidence those guys have. They have taken confidence from the dynamics of what we did against Dundee at the weekend. The conviction in both boxes was there tonight and that’s key for us to take into the next run of games.’.

Vrancken had no real complaint with Monaco’s penalty, awarded for a foul by Jamie McCart on Matthis Abline, but was unhappy that German referee Daniel Schlager failed to spot a foul on Kerjota before the visitors’ second goal.

Hearts players revel in the celebrations after Kerjota's wondergoal sent Tynecastle wild.

Recent findings suggest that ‘For me, the penalty was light but okay,’ added the Belgian. ‘But if you are really decisive to give a penalty there, then you don’t see one of our players having his shirt pulled in the build-up to their second goal, that’s frustrating.

‘At this level, things can happen like this. It wasn’t given for us and it wasn’t the only decision like that tonight.’.

Monaco coach Filipe Luis revelled in his team’s late win but admitted even he felt like joining in the acclamation of Kerjota’s goal for Hearts.

Sources indicate that ‘Hearts were a tough opponent and I knew it would be difficult,’ stated Luis. ‘We found spaces and created chances from the start but Hearts scored a fantastic goal to go ahead.

‘But we stayed calm and scored twice before they scored another fantastic goal. It was so good, I almost had to applaud it!

‘Hearts didn’t create many chances in the second half and in the end we managed to win, so there are many good things for us tonight.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a newly introduced MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

While the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

It has been revealed that the Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

In Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

The parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an problem in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

In the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. As long as that's the case, I'm rarely going to bet against the Herons.

In a recent development, now the playoffs really are getting underway. These are one-off games where the best of the best are going up against each other. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

Okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Participants: Vancouver Whitecaps, Inter MiamiWinners: Inter Miami.

Hey, it's Messi and Muller, just like we're having a top-tier Champions League matchup. It has been a playoff gauntlet, but the more things change, the more they stay the same. Muller and Messi have faced each other 11 times, with Muller claiming seven wins to Messi's four. However, after getting one over on Muller last season, Messi isn't going to let a chance at a second consecutive MLS Cup pass by, even if this one is in Vancouver amid the uncertain future of BC Place as the home of the Whitecaps.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.

"There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak said after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

"The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".

The threat comes after the Canadian government confirmed Wednesday that it would not allow Russian players to take part in the IIHF World Junior Championship starting on December 26 in Alberta.

"Canada's position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues ⁠its war of aggression ​against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual," Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary of sport, remarked in a statement on Wednesday. "Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.".

Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling in late October, in which it stated the security concerns the IIHF cited for barring Russian teams from taking part in international tournaments was not sufficient, the world governing body pledged to work to comply with the decision.

On November 8, Norway said it had been bumped from the World Juniors tournament and had been informed by the IIHF that Russia would take its place. Several other national hockey associations said they had received a revised schedule for the tournament and stated they would not play against Russia. The IIHF has not confirmed the change.

Germany has been watching developments related to the World Juniors and host nation Canada closely, as it is set to host the IIHF World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf starting on May 14.

With several nations saying they will not play Russia and major sponsors threatening to pull out, a German government spokesman described the prospect of hosting the tournament under these conditions as "effectively impossible.".

However, Germany has ruled out taking the Canadian approach.

Ronald Rauhe, Germany's minister of state for sport, stated Wednesday that refusing to grant visas was "not a solution for the [German] ice hockey federation [DEB], nor is it a solution for successfully hosting a world championship anywhere.".

At the same time, though, he expressed support for the DEB in its wish to host the tournament as planned.

"We believe that we should channel all our energy and efforts into helping sport — and ice hockey in particular — find a solution, which would, of course, entail excluding Russia from the World Championship.".

What makes things even more complicated for German officials are concerns that taking a hard-line on Russia could jeopardize Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

In a recent development, the thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees bidding to host an Olympic Games to follow its lead. The IOC is set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process.

Sources indicate that for now, though, the ball appears to be in the IIHF's court, after Ottawa confirmed its refusal to grant Russians visas to play in the World Juniors. How the dispute regarding that tournament gets resolved could go a long way to finding a solution for the men's tournament in Germany in May.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino must now know that defender Harry Maguire is undroppable.

With Pochettino setting up for his first game as Manchester United manager against Liverpool in the Premier League, he made the bold decision to start Matthijs de Ligt at centre-back.

That meant that experienced defender Maguire was on the bench, which was certainly an interesting decision, given how long de Ligt had been out for.

You could certainly argue that Maguire has been part of a terrible defence this whole season, but playing de Ligt ahead of him was certainly not the answer.

The Dutch defender looked completely out of sorts and not fit enough, and Pochettino must have regretted his decision to start him, even in the opening 10 minutes.

De Ligt dropped to the bench for United's game against Sporting CP in the Champions League during the week.

Although they drew 2-2 with the Portuguese side, they certainly looked more assured defensively, giving up just 0.7 xG from open play.

Mistakes at the back were incredibly costly for Pochettino's side, and Maguire was certainly one who wasn't to blame.

Pochettino must have realised now that Maguire could be one of the undroppable ones in his starting eleven.

Defensively, United have been atrocious so far this season, but maybe Maguire isn't the problem. The experienced centre-back has been playing alongside the likes of Lisandro Martinez, who has endured a difficult season and been the subject of a telling Ben Jacobs patch on his Man Utd future, Ayden Heaven, who has shown plenty of inexperience, and Leny Yoro, who has made a lot of mistakes.

Against Sporting, Maguire won all of his ground duels and all of his aerial duels, whilst also completing four long balls.

He won everything at the back and was let down by his teammates, in particular Senne Lammens between the sticks.

The likes of Bruno Fernandes are certainly undroppable, given he's capable of producing moments of magic, while Yoro was also a rock at the back against Sporting.

Many have suggested that these two are two of the undroppable ones for Pochettino, but Maguire could be creeping his way in.

Maguire is certainly a better option for United than de Ligt, Heaven, and even Martinez.

Although many will be suggesting that Maguire isn't the answer long term due to his age, which is certainly true, he still could be the answer in the short term.

United can't completely reshuffle their defence until the transfer window opens, and even then, they're unlikely to sign more than one player.

Maguire's experience and leadership could be crucial for United over the coming months, and although he's been part of a terrible defence, he certainly doesn't appear to be the issue.

Pochettino must now know that Maguire is one of his undroppable players, and he shouldn't be making the mistake again of starting de Ligt ahead of him.

Science’s greatest failure is not getting things wrong, but by sometimes pretending that there is more certainty than there really is, indicates social scientist Andy Stirling.

This can happen, he claims, when researchers face political pressure to provide a single, definitive answer, when the evidence is far more complex.

In the final episode of a six-part podcast series about failure in science, Stirling, an emeritus professor at the University of Sussex in Brighton, UK, draws on examples from climate change, the COVID-19 pandemic, environmental campaigns and energy policy.

Sources indicate that “In those areas, science just does not convey the degree of uncertainty and of variability and of how many potentially viable options are being cut out when you just give one clear answer,” he states. “It thinks it’s helping society by just giving one picture of the truth. And in fact, it’s undermining both itself and democracy when it does that.”.

Stirling, whose research includes science and technology policy and environmental politics, says that on occasions politicians have almost literally hidden behind scientists on a podium, who have relied on their authority and expertise to protect them.

When it pretends that’s not the case, it is in fact behaving in a post-truth way, and so then it’s not surprising it gets a post-truth reaction.

So doubling down on that is exactly...it’s like throwing kerosene on the fire. It’s just not going to work to. Your self behaving in this authoritarian way and expect other authoritarianisms to go away.

We should be informing democracy and achieving these changes through democratic struggle. And science is absolutely essential to that, but only if it conducts itself in an honest way.

One thing that got me going with all this was in back in the ’90 s I was looking at risk assessments, cost-benefit analysis, life cycle assessments.

All these highly technical quantitative assessments in the energy sector.

In a recent development, cutting a long story short, they were, the energy sector was the place where these things were developed to their most mature, sophisticated form. And if you looked at any given study, you got this really confident idea.

This is what the risks of nuclear are compared to renewables, compared to gas, or whatever it is.

The same with the other methods I mentioned.

And then every single time you stand back and you look at the literature as a whole, not just peer-reviewed literature, but the literature embodied in law.

So the most kind of authoritatively treated source of data on these things, and you found you could get any answer you like across that peer-reviewed literature.

It depends on the framing. The models give you an answer that depends on how you frame the question.

And that for me kind of radicalized me because I realized that none of the committees, none of the reports around the world were fully representing what the literature they were consulting told us, that you can get all kinds of different answers.

And what matters is not just the one answer, the risk, the cost, environmental costs, the ecosystem service.

What matters is how that changes depending on assumptions, that’s how science should speak to policy, but also to society, telling us how these things depend.

The reason I remarked that, a lot of people talk about lamenting the fact we have policy-based evidence rather than evidence-based policy, and it’s a good point.

You know, you get all kinds of practices making things up all the time, all over the place in every sector.

In a recent development, but my point wasn’t to lambast that. It wasn’t to say, to lament yet again "you guys are just stitching it up." It was to say "Actually, I’ve never yet seen an area where the evidence compels a single policy.".

So even when you do get the best quality evidence, it is never without uncertainties. It’s never without differences of implication for action, depending on which discipline was actually most influential, how the questions were asked, what the baselines were, etc. etc.

So I have yet to see any body of analysis based on evidence that compels a single decision.

So when you hear people talking about evidence-based policy as if there were only one policy that could have been based on the evidence, they’re basically again being post-truth.

They’re (to be a bit more colourful about it, they’re telling porkies.".

In a recent development, because there will always be values, interests, assumptions at work, and it’s not a bad thing. It’s inevitable.

It has been revealed that that’s how science, you know, depends. For instance, on BSE whether vets or were the epidemiologists in charge? He got a very different answer.

In a recent development, and in COVID, you know, again, we-I mean, it’s still too early to say, as Mao said, I think about the French Revolution, was it? But it’s too early to say.

But you can still see that what was the best way to act on the available evidence, economic as well as epidemiological, and the different ways of interpreting the epidemiological evidence.

It’s very clear now that it’s not so clear-cut what a particular country should do.

Different countries do different things. There are different ways of looking back on it, looking at the time and seeing what was good and what was bad.

So, without taking position on either side, it’s far from clear that there was a single definitive action that should have been taken.

I defy anyone to actually come back and defend that. There’ll be a matter of judgment as between really quite radically different policies.

So COVID is an example of this. I think we had to pretend there was one policy because it was so stressful.

Politicians had to pretend because otherwise they would have to hide behind their chief scientists, literally sometimes, literally behind them on the podium, hiding behind them because they needed that authority to protect them from the inevitable uncertainties that everyone believed were really there, even though they weren’t acknowledging it in the graphs.

I mean, blame management, trust, public acceptance.

These things are the most crucial commodities in politics. So yeah, and it’s you know apocryphally, people have all kinds of anecdotes out on these advisory committees.

In a recent development, I’ve served a little bit on some of them. You know, the number of times in which the politicians will intimate, "I won’t hesitate to hide behind you," almost as a joke.

Sources indicate that but so you know, scientists respond to that in different ways. But by and large, they think, "Well, okay, we’ve got to be responsible. Let’s give these guys a single prescriptive answer, even though we know among ourselves that we could have got a different answer, but we’ve got a responsibility not to do an to do to do an elevator pitch.".

Recent findings suggest that you know, not to give on the one hand, on the other, as Margaret Thatcher remarked, "Save me from the two-handed economist. I want a one-handed economist.".

Industry observers note that she wants it because of justification, but actually, it’s a responsibility of the economist, or in this case, a scientist, to actually explain how it does depend. It always does depend.

If they don’t explain that, then they are failing, I would say science, and failing society, failing democracy.

Sources indicate that other things are really complicated. there’s a lot of real challenges. I don’t want to pretend it’s easier than it really is.

But actually, we shouldn’t be paralyzed by this. Look at science itself. When it developed in the 17th century, motto of the Royal Society, nullius in verba, that was basically saying that principles of accountability, of argument, of deliberation really mattered, of treating people more equally than many institutions do. That’s not the opposite of democracy. That is democracy.

Science was about, in many ways, democratizing knowledge.

You know, you needed to argue, you need to show evidence and do analyzes in rigorous ways. But it should be open to anyone to do that, and to any perspective, no matter how ridiculous it sounds, if it can substantiate itself.

So science and democracy are not on opposite sides.

So I think, rather than counterpointing them, like science is against democracy, we can’t trust democracy, going to undermine science, actually, see it the other way round: that science is an embodiment of democracy.

It’s when it is at its best. It’s when it’s being democratic about the ability to challenge power inside science, and that’s how we solve the problems of science.

It’s also how we solve the problems at the moment of democracy, which science is, sadly, because it’s forced to be more authoritarian in pretending a singular truth.

It’s forced into that not by democracy, but by power that is also eroding democracy.

So I think the answer is democracy.

Science, when it comes to advise policymakers, yes, please do your best, but don’t think of yourself just giving a single expedient answer so that a politician goes away happy and can act without worrying about blame.

Inform society at large about the assumptions that went into that.

Show how it depends, and if you do that, you’re informing democracy as much as the powerful actors who are, you know, maybe conferring the patronage on the scientists.

Science fails when it’s not being plural enough.

It needs to be plural about who’s involved, about the questions that are asked, about the disciplines that get around the table, about how it conveys its interpretations of its understandings out to society, and it needs to just not be scared of representing that plurality because with that comes the conditions.

It’s not just anything goes. It’s not plural for plurality’s sake.

It’s then saying under what conditions you get answer X or answer Y, and that’s more scientific.

It’s more rigorous to behave in that way.

In a recent development, when science does that, it’s being more scientific when it’s plural. So I think science fails most when it reduces all those kinds of plurality.

To just a singular idea of truth.

Breaking: What's going on with the polar vortex?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons.
  • If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.
  • Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons. This is the polar vortex.

If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.

Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.

It's not yet clear how the current disruption to the polar vortex will affect the Northern Hemisphere winter, but scientists agree it is a record-breaking event.

"As far as we know, this is the earliest stratospheric vortex disruption that has been observed," European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecast (ECMWF) principal scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart told the AFP news agency.

The French meteorological agency Meteo-France, meanwhile, called it "an unprecedented event.".

The early breakdown of the vortex "really increases the chance of cold air outbreaks across the latitudes where most of the densely populated population centers are across the Northern Hemisphere, US, Europe and East Asia," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology told AFP.

The polar vortex is an enormous band of cold, low-pressure air that spins counterclockwise around the North Pole, about 10 to 50 kilometers (around 6 to 30 miles) above the surface.

Sources indicate that it's closely connected to the jet stream, another band of powerful winds just below the vortex. The jet stream forms a boundary where the cold Arctic air meets warmer air from the tropics and subtropics.

Recent findings suggest that the vortex can sometimes be a tight circle, keeping the coldest air locked around the North Pole over winter. It can also form uneven waves that dip southwards. And as it changes in strength and shape, that can influence the atmosphere below and alter the position of the jet stream, which drives the weather on the ground.

So, if the jet stream is more "wavy," and plunges south, it may also allow freezing Arctic air to spill southward.

One of the biggest influences that can provoke this kind of disruption is known as "sudden stratospheric warming." This is when temperatures in the polar stratosphere rise dramatically within a few days, causing the vortex's strong westerly winds to weaken.

This can push the vortex off its spot at the North Pole, make it split apart into multiple rings, or — as is happening now — cause the westerly winds to change direction.

It can take several weeks for the vortex to recover.

A previous polar vortex disruption contributed to the deadly Great Texas Freeze in February 2021, which caused more than a week of freezing temperatures that sparked power outages and killed hundreds of people.

According to recent reports, but bone-chilling cold isn't a foregone conclusion. The Met Office, which is the UK's national weather and climate service, stresses that what's happening with the polar vortex can nudge odds in that direction, but it's not a switch that turns cold weather on and off.

Other weather patterns can also influence the outcome.

For example, there's a possibility El Nino, which is associated with milder winters, could "moderate or modify" the impacts, Cohen told AFP. But he added this was not certain.

The El Nino weather phenomenon, caused by the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is currently intensifying and is expected to peak at the end of the year. The ongoing event has been classified as exceptionally strong and is disrupting weather around the globe.

Some research has also linked the rapid warming of the Arctic driven by climate change to increasing disruptions to the polar vortex. That means that, even as the planet warms, some areas may still experience more severe cold spells. But this connection is not conclusive and is still debated by scientists.

Martin O’Neill hailed ‘magnificent’ Camilo Duran for helping Celtic win ugly against Torreense to keep their Europa League dream alive.

The Parkhead men looked to be in for a rare comfortable night on the road when Torreense defender Javi Vazquez scored an own goal after nine minutes.

But sloppy defending by the visitors allowed the Portuguese to level 10 minutes later through Dany Jean.

With the minnows sitting in and hoping for a point late on, though, veteran James Forrest climbed off the bench to set up fellow sub Duran for his 15th goal of the season.

On the late impact of the Colombian, O’Neill stated: ‘I think you always have to keep the faith. But we were gambling almost everything. They were camped outside their penalty area and we were hoping at some stage or another somebody might come up with something.

‘And of course, once again, Duran has done it. He is just a magnificent footballer.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill praised Camilo Duran for once again riding to the rescue.

In a recent development, ‘Fifteen goals and we’re not into December yet. He’s been flying, he’s a terrific player, there’s no question about it.

‘That’s two games he’s come up substantial for us as well (on back of Besiktas). Maybe 22 games, in all honesty. But he’s been great. He didn’t start the game although we knew he could come on.’.

Although delighted with the result, O’Neill was the first to admit that the performance was not all it might have been.

‘Despite the fact that we’d plenty of possession, I thought that we should just accelerate once or twice, not only just into their half, but also be more penetrative,’ he added.

Sources indicate that ‘And I think that was the point. I thought we had a lot of ball in the second half as well.

‘There’s always a possibility on the break that you could concede but we had to take the chance because the three points tonight were of vital importance.

‘But, yeah, there’s lots that we can still do to improve our game.’.

Duran's downward header sealed the points for Celtic and ignited their qualification hopes.

The dramatic outcome ensured Celtic are now up to 25th place in the 36-team group – from 32nd – after losing their opening three matches.

O’Neill’s men next face Omonia with Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise to come in January.

‘I’m just delighted to have won — it keeps us going,’ added O’Neill. ‘We’ve got six points on the board and we’ve still got a couple of games to go.

‘So, from an absolutely almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we’ve given ourselves some hope.’.

Celtic’s star man on the night, Jota set up the opening goal and relished the return to his homeland almost two years after his last European match.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s been a long time that I wanted to come back to Portugal and play in front of my friends and family,’ he remarked. ‘And there’s no better way than with a win with three points. It was something that we wanted to achieve today and luckily we did it.

‘It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible. And right now it’s all about enjoying. There’s no expectation — just to be a professional, having the responsibility of being a Celtic player and delivering every day.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

According to recent reports, “Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found glitch had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.
